outlook: Grains were mostly lower in overnight trade as of about 7:30 a.m. CT on Election Day: December corn was down 4¼ cents at $4.44, January soybeans down 3 cents at $12.13¾, December Minneapolis spring wheat down 2½ cents at $6.23¼ and Chicago wheat down 4¾ cents at $6.01¾, while January canola fell C$9.10 to C$779.30. USDA's Monday Crop Progress report put corn harvest at 74% complete (vs. 60% a week earlier and a 77% five-year average) and soybean harvest at 94%. Crude oil recovered about 2% after Monday's plunge, following reports of U.S. strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, and traders are awaiting midterm election results that could shape the farm bill. Steady rain is forecast over the Northern Plains and upper Midwest today.

news.title: First Thing Today | Will markets find their footing after Election Day?
Wheat and corn rise, while soybeans fall in Chicago on Monday
